name: Rania Haddad
headline: 28, part-time university tutor and freelance translator, Amman
title: An Interruption at the Kitchen Table
situation: Rania is at the kitchen table, spreading jam on a slice of bread and arranging her translation notes for the evening, when a knock comes at the door. It is one of her students, a quiet young man who attends her kitchen-table tutorials, holding a crumpled draft. He apologizes for coming unannounced, but his essay is due tomorrow and he cannot figure out how to fix the thesis. He says he won't stay long. Rania sees his worn notebook and remembers he once mentioned a broken printer. The bread is still in her hand. The bus ride home is already behind her, and her translation work sits open on the table.

context.relationship_profiles:
The student is a regular attendee of her kitchen-table tutorials, usually arriving with borrowed textbooks and apologizing for taking her time.
He once told her his printer broke, and she lent him a spare copy of her notes; they've had a few short conversations about his writing struggles.
He is respectful and rarely asks for help, so an unannounced visit suggests real urgency.
context.tendencies:
When students show up unexpectedly at her table, she has set aside her own work to untangle their drafts, often making tea and cutting bread.
She has repeatedly rearranged evening translation hours to accommodate students who face deadlines.
She avoids turning anyone away who sits down with a notebook, even when her own schedule is tight.
context.current_state:
She is tired from a full day of teaching and the commute, but the bread and jam routine is her usual way of settling into evening work.
Her translation ledger is open, with a legal document due by morning.
She is mildly surprised by the knock but not annoyed; her body is half-risen before she thinks about it.
context.immediate_memories:
The crumpled draft and worn notebook remind her of the student's earlier comment about his broken printer, and of giving him a spare copy of her lecture notes.
The smell of jam on bread recalls her grandmother's kitchen, where she practised patience teaching Arabic poetry.
The sound of the knock at the kitchen table reminds her of other evenings when students arrived with last-minute requests after she had finished her own plans.
context.reflective_memories:
She remembers many nights when she put aside translation to read a rough draft, then stayed up later to finish her own work.
She has seen students grow when they get one clear explanation; she believes in the value of showing up even when it costs her time.
She knows her own words were once ignored, and she has made a habit of listening carefully to students' hesitations.
